kicker: Whisper, with a subspace projected out

scenes.headline: How to project Whisper's hallucinations out of its decoder
scenes.sub: A low-rank subspace, found from non-speech audio, subtracted at inference.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Praline! Play Whisper a rooster, and it writes: I'm the best. Here's how one paper removes that failure without changing a single weight.

scenes.text: Find the directions in Whisper's decoder that separate hallucinating from staying silent on non-speech audio, and subtract them at inference.
scenes.say: It's the abliteration move, aimed at a failure mode instead of a safeguard. Find the direction behind the hallucination, and subtract it while decoding.

items.say: Run plain Whisper on twelve hundred clips with no speech in them.
Pair the clips where it hallucinated with ones where it stayed silent, and subtract their decoder states.
Take the SVD, and keep the top few directions: one for the small model, four for the large.

scenes.title: The edit, at inference
scenes.say: At inference, one line does the work.

parts.note: the part of the state inside the subspace
parts.say: This is the part of each decoder state that lies in the hallucination subspace.

parts.note: how much to remove; 1 removes it all
parts.say: Alpha sets how much comes out. No weights change, and no gradient step runs.

scenes.title: Only edit when Whisper already doubts

steps.say: Editing every input would also edit real speech. So first, one plain pass reads Whisper's own no-speech probability.
Only if that clears a low gate does Whisper decode again, with the projection hooked in.
Either way, Whisper's usual threshold of point six decides: keep the text, or return nothing.

scenes.label: non-speech hallucination rate, averaged over three model scales and three benchmarks
scenes.note: gated projection still raises LibriSpeech WER by 0.33 to 4.39 points
scenes.say: Averaged over three model sizes and three benchmarks, hallucination on non-speech falls from thirty-one point three percent to two point four. The bill arrives as word errors on real speech.

scenes.text: A low-rank edit found from 1,200 clips cuts non-speech hallucination sharply, and it is paid for in word error rate.
scenes.mark: paid for in word error rate

recap: Contrast hallucinated and silent decoder states
Project that subspace out at inference
Gate it, and pay in word errors
scenes.say: To recap: contrast, project, gate, and count the cost in word errors.
